15import logging 

16 

17import triton 

18import triton.language as tl 

19from _kunlunxin.utils.codegen_config_utils import CodeGenConfig 

20 

21from ..utils.pointwise_dynamic import pointwise_dynamic 

22 

23logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

24 

25config_ = CodeGenConfig( 

26 512, 

27 (65536, 65536, 65536), 

28 32, 

29 True, 

30 prefer_1d_tile=True, 

31 # ALWAYS_BOOL output -> keep isCloseMemoryAsync at its DEFAULT (True = async 

32 # copy closed). Opening async (=False) on a bool op re-introduces the 

33 # ConvertTritonXPUToLLVM giant-struct explosion on top of buffer_size_limit 

34 # (same trap as logical_or/and/xor). 

35 # 

36 # buffer_size_limit=4096 + unroll_num=16 keeps the per-unroll chunk at 

37 # 4096/16 == 256 elements (identical to the previous 2048/8 == 256, so the 

38 # monolithic-struct explosion is still avoided) but doubles the in-flight 

39 # buffer, which measurably raises large-shape DMA throughput: on XPU the 

40 # big shapes ([4096,4096], [1024,65536], [64,64,4096]) get a stable ~8% 

41 # latency drop across fp16/fp32/bf16 vs the old unroll_num=8 / default 

42 # (2048) buffer. Small shapes stay launch-floor bound (unchanged). 

43 # 

44 # kunlunAutoGrid=True for the single-CTA config: the 1-CTA path (numel 

45 # <= 131072) is faster for tiny shapes, and >= 16384 elements is covered 

46 # by the multi-CTA config below (hybrid dispatch, see logical_not()). 

47 kunlunAutoGrid=True, 

48 unroll_num=16, 

49 buffer_size_limit=4096, 

50) 

51 

52config_multi_ = CodeGenConfig( 

53 512, 

54 (65536, 65536, 65536), 

55 32, 

56 True, 

57 prefer_1d_tile=True, 

58 kunlunAutoGrid=False, 

59 unroll_num=16, 

60 buffer_size_limit=4096, 

61) 

62 

63# Shapes below this numel keep the 1-CTA (kunlunAutoGrid=True) kernel; larger 

64# shapes switch to the constant 12-CTA kernel. A/B measured 2026-10-19 on the 

65# benchmark matrix: (64,64)/(64,64,1) and (1024,1) are 2-5x FASTER at 1-CTA 

66# (5.7/5.5/5.3us vs 10.6/10.6/26.3us) while (1024,16), (64,64,16) and every 

67# >= 262144-element shape are 1.2-2.2x faster at 12-CTA (6.8->5.5us, 

68# 11.7->6.1us, 155->126us @16.7M for fp16). 

69_MULTI_CTA_MIN_NUMEL = 16384

72@triton.jit 

73def _logical_not_body(x): 

74 # `logical_not(x)` == `(x == 0)`. For float inputs a bitcast-icmp body is 

75 # used instead of an fp compare: XPU has no fast per-element `x != 0` in fp, 

76 # a floating-point compare (cmpf) lowered to i1 costs ~2x a plain icmp 

77 # (measured on XPU 7, 2026-08-13: [4096,4096] fp16 ~0.49ms for 

78 # `not x.to(tl.int1)` vs ~0.24ms for the bitcast-icmp body; [1024,65536] 

79 # 1.60ms vs 0.64ms; same ratio for fp32/bf16; re-verified 2026-10-19 on 

80 # XPU 4: fp16-domain `x == 0.0` is ~2.0x slower than the icmp body). 

81 # u = bitcast(x, <same-width int>) -- fp16 -> i16 (no widening!) 

82 # (u & signmask) == 0 -- true only for +/-0.0 

83 # All other bit patterns, incl. NaN/inf/subnormals, are non-zero after the 

84 # sign mask -> False. Result matches torch.logical_not bit-exactly for all 

85 # float edge cases (NaN, +/-inf, -0.0, subnormals) verified on-device. 

86 # 

87 # fp16 (and only fp16) stays in 16-bit arithmetic: the i16 bitcast-icmp is 

88 # ~1.8-2.4x faster than the fp32-upcast round trip (micro-benchmark 

89 # 2026-10-19: 16.7M elems 671us -> 373us; 67M 2633us -> 1465us), simply 

90 # because the per-element fp16->fp32 conversion is skipped. bf16 must keep 

91 # the fp32 upcast: the same-width `x.to(tl.int16, bitcast=True)` fails to 

92 # compile on this backend (TritonXPUDtypeConvert: "Cannot bitcast 

93 # data-type of size 32 to data-type of size 16"), and fp32 cannot bitcast 

94 # down to i16 at all. The integer/bool paths use a direct integer compare. 

95 if tl.constexpr(x.dtype.is_fp32()): 

96 u = x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) 

97 return (u & 0x7FFFFFFF) == 0 

98 elif tl.constexpr(x.dtype.is_fp16()): 

99 u = x.to(tl.int16, bitcast=True) 

100 return (u & 0x7FFF) == 0 

101 elif tl.constexpr(x.dtype.is_bf16()): 

102 u = x.to(tl.float32).to(tl.int32, bitcast=True) 

103 return (u & 0x7FFFFFFF) == 0 

104 else: 

105 return x == 0 

106 

107 

108@pointwise_dynamic(promotion_methods=[(0, "ALWAYS_BOOL")], config=config_) 

109@triton.jit 

110def logical_not_func(x): 

111 return _logical_not_body(x) 

112 

113 

114# Duplicate of logical_not_func with the constant 12-CTA config. The two 

115# functions must be distinct @triton.jit functions (distinct source text) so 

116# the in-process codegen cache can hold both variants side by side. 

117@pointwise_dynamic(promotion_methods=[(0, "ALWAYS_BOOL")], config=config_multi_) 

118@triton.jit 

119def logical_not_func_multi_cta(x): 

120 return _logical_not_body(x) 

121 

122 

123def logical_not(A): 

124 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN LOGICAL_NOT") 

125 if A.numel() < _MULTI_CTA_MIN_NUMEL: 

126 return logical_not_func(A) 

127 return logical_not_func_multi_cta(A) 

128 

129 

130def logical_not_(A): 

131 # In-place variant was NOT overridden -> fell back to the generic 

132 # ops/logical_not.py path with the default pointwise_dynamic config (tile 512, 

133 # buffer_size_limit=2048, no unroll/autoGrid) -> catastrophic (38-161ms on 

134 # large shapes, speedup ~0.001-0.005). Reuse the now-tuned logical_not_func 

135 # with out0=A (same recipe as bitwise_not_), same hybrid dispatch. 

136 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN LOGICAL_NOT_") 

137 if A.numel() < _MULTI_CTA_MIN_NUMEL: 

138 logical_not_func(A, out0=A) 

139 else: 

140 logical_not_func_multi_cta(A, out0=A) 

141 return A
